situation:
You are the human resources manager for WILLOW BEND CARE COMMUNITIES, an operator of four skilled nursing homes. The regional vice president (judge), who took the company over a year ago after two years of losses, has asked to meet with you about the way nursing aides and dining staff are scheduled.

The turnaround plan has held wages steady and frozen new labor spending. Resident census swings week to week. On light weeks the homes carry aides with little to do and the kitchens plate meals for residents who have already been discharged, and on heavy weeks those same aides are asked to stay over at overtime rates. Both waste money the plan cannot spare.

A scheduling model used elsewhere in the industry would release each week's shifts to aides two days ahead, sized to the census. State labor rules permit it, and it would cut the overtime and the discarded food together. At its last meeting the family council said plainly that families want their relatives cared for by faces the residents recognize.

Under shifts released two days ahead, families would meet a different aide most days, and the aides who cannot arrange childcare on that notice are the ones most likely to quit; they are also the staff the turnaround needs. Keeping fixed assignments preserves the continuity the families ask for, but leaves the overtime and the discarded food on the books.

The regional vice president (judge) wants you to analyze what the company owes its residents' families and its aides, recommend how the homes should schedule, and describe how the recommendation would be carried out and explained. The regional vice president (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the regional vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the regional vice president (judge) at WILLOW BEND CARE COMMUNITIES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the human resources manager to recommend whether the homes should release shifts two days ahead against the census or keep fixed assignments, to say plainly what each choice costs the aides, the families and the turnaround, and to describe how the recommendation would actually be put in place.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: If we start next month, what happens in the first two weeks?
